correctness.rationale: The row KL projection is an exponential tilt, preserving √(u_-u_+)/u_0; for means ±a the same strictly increasing Q_a fixes the common endpoint total r and gives reflected rows for arbitrary strictly positive input weights. Column rescaling changes the projective invariant by T(1−r)/[(1−T)r]; row multipliers and martingale tilts persist as gauges. Entropy strict convexity and reflection identify π_T as the unique optimum, not the only feasible joint law. For z=log q the cycle derivative is a²(1−r)/[r(r−a²)] in (0,1) with limit 1 as r↓a. The map is increasing and its increment has sign T−r, giving global monotone trapping and a unique fixed point; the derivative at r=T gives the exact asymptotic ratio in both coordinates. The forward KL divergence to π_T vanishes quadratically with positive second derivative T/(T²−a²)+1/(1−T), giving the squared ratio on nonstationary trajectories only (at a stationary initialization the displayed ratio is undefined). Finally 1−λ=(T²−a²)/[T(T−a²)] gives the fixed-a boundary coefficient, not a claim about the iteration at T=a. The supporting checker was inspected but not run; these are symbolic deductions, not an extrapolation from its seeded tests.
